# Private clinical documents and explicit public images — amended draft

13 November 2026. Author: internal Codex `/root/lab_remaining_audit`. PREPARATION ONLY; no self-approval. Supersedes draft SHAac312cae after actual Standards/Spec REQUEST_CHANGES archived in `output/qa/private-clinical-documents/CONTRACT_REVIEW_INITIAL.json`. No source edit or execution is authorized until two actual nonauthor decisions bind these exact amended bytes. R9 selected inputs remain untouched.

## Full S1 milestone and the first implementation boundary

S1 still requires authorized clinical bytes, immutable original/corrected versions, genuine public-image compatibility, all legacy static/fetch aliases closed to unauthorized clinical access, migrated available legacy bytes with history unknown, bounded authenticated provider acquisition, and qualified clinical validation/release and supported-client behavior. Staging a prerequisite does not remove any of that scope or close the existing public-document defect.

The FIRST increment is deliberately frozen: asset/version identities and metadata; owned private/unbound and resource-bound upload commands; exclusive private object storage; private version listing/content reads; scanner/release eligibility ports; append-only audit admission; unbound revocation; and minimal legacy file-path isolation preventing legacy aliases/writers/deleters from reaching the NEW private subtree. It does not change existing public image endpoints/fields, republish old assets, integrate providers, migrate legacy records or claim qualified clinical flow completion. Full static cutover, public writer/client adapters, existing booking/provider write adapters, clinical policy/scanner adapters and clinical detach/release are pending dependent S1 phases, not declared implemented by this prerequisite.

Reuse the existing file module, AppError, authenticated file router, formidable and existing booking repositories. No generic workflow engine, new identity service, duplicated booking system, new package or root startup change. Source ownership for the first increment: `src1/modules/file/{routes,controller,services,types}/index.ts`; new `documents.ts`, `documentTypes.ts`, `storage.ts`, `model/index.ts`, `repository/index.ts`, `validation/index.ts` under that module. Existing FileService upload/delete and FileController pathname methods change ONLY their private-subtree/path guards. Their ordinary public-image response adapters are byte-preserved. No booking/external-booking/provider source edit in the first increment. A later exact adapter contract owns those files.

## Frozen identity and normalized data

All IDs from an HTTP actor/route are primitive exact24hex strings without trim/coercion; canonical storage is lowercase24hex. Source-generated ObjectIds are not accepted as caller-selected asset/version IDs. In the first increment actor kind is exactly `user`; authenticated admin/HR/pharmacy/specialist callers are403 `DOCUMENT_ACTOR_FORBIDDEN`, not new clinical staff. The central authenticate401 retains precedence. Actor identity is a signed account ID, never a phone/email, corporate or linked business ID.

A trusted scope resolver returns exactly `{resourceKind, resourceId, ownerUserId}`. Kinds are `unbound_upload|booking|external_booking`. For unbound, resourceId=ownerUserId=signed user ID. For booking/external_booking, perform an exact scoped repository query with literal ID and mandatory scalar stored userId equality; absent/foreign404 `DOCUMENT_NOT_FOUND`. No optional owner, raw-filter spread, current userId hints, dependent ID or URL reference grants access. Resource authority must be read from the matching current stored row. The first increment does not expose a general client-supplied purpose/owner/source interface.

Stable logical asset identity is SHA256 of UTF8 JSON.stringify of this ordered ARRAY, without whitespace: `["sd-file-asset:v1", resourceKind, resourceId, ownerUserId, sourceSystem, sourceDocumentReference]`. sourceSystem enum is `owned_upload|labstack|healthians|legacy_import`. The tuple is stored alongside its lowercase64hex identityKey and compared on every collision; the hash alone is never authorization. The stable server-derived candidate assetId is ObjectId(identityKey.slice(0,24)), so concurrent first observations resolve the same asset before any version write. A prefix collision with a different FULL stored identity is409, never an ownerless adoption or regenerated second asset. This predictable identifier is not an access token; only the generated32byte storage filename is a secret object locator. Inside the capture transaction, insert the new revision0 asset if absent or compare the complete existing tuple; the unique identity/_id race aborts before the bounded fresh reconciliation transaction. Different loser version files remain private unreachable orphans. No separately committed asset reservation or undocumented audit phase is needed. For owned upload sourceDocumentReference is the caller's UUIDv4 documentKey (canonical lowercase UUID) scoped by current owner/resource. It names a logical document, not an asset ID or storage filename. One UUID per file; exactly one file/request in this increment. Retrying the same logical documentKey MUST resolve the same asset before version dedupe. A different documentKey means a different logical asset, even if bytes match.

Provider/legacy references are reserved internal source values only: bounded1–256 UTF8 bytes, exact nonempty strings with no C0/DEL or leading/trailing whitespace. Preserve opaque case and Unicode bytes; no lowercasing, trimming or NFC folding of provider identifiers. Unknown reference is not fabricated as a global common value: acquisition is503 until its source adapter can supply a stable reference. Provider account/integration namespace must be included in the future provider sourceDocumentReference contract; current enums alone do not establish provider-account scope. Those live adapters are excluded from the first increment.

`FileAsset` fields: schemaVersion1; server _id; exact stored identity tuple/identityKey; purpose `private_attachment|clinical_document|public_image`; resourceKind/resourceId/ownerUserId; server createdByUserId/createdAt; integer revision>=0; currentCapturedVersionId|null; currentReadableVersionId|null; revokedAt|null. Purpose is assigned by the service command: unbound upload→private_attachment; owned booking upload→clinical_document. Purpose and identity are immutable. Public_image is RESERVED, rejected by the first-increment public/HTTP/service commands; no current arbitrary imageUrl/profilePictureUrl promotes assets. Assets whose resource now resolves to a different owner deny503 `DOCUMENT_SCOPE_CHANGED`; do not reassign their owner or grant the new account the old bytes automatically.

`FileAssetVersion` immutable capture fields: server _id=versionId; assetId; identityKey; storageKey; contentSha256; actualSize(1..10MiB); mediaType enum PDF/JPEG/PNG/WebP; sourceSystem/sourceDocumentReference copied from asset; sourceVersionLabel `{kind:"unknown"}` or `{kind:"recorded",value:string}`; sourceStageLabel with the same tagged form; completeness `preliminary|final|unknown`; amendsVersionId|null; amendmentReason|null; capturedAt/createdByUserId assigned on FIRST successful capture. Recorded label/reason strings are exact1..256 UTF8 bytes, no C0/DEL or boundary whitespace; absent labels normalize to taggedunknown, never empty-string sentinels. No clinical completeness/label/correction fields are accepted from first-increment HTTP uploads: they use unknown/unknown/unknown/null/null. Corrections with an explicit previous version are future qualified source adapters.

Version identity is SHA256 of UTF8 compact JSON.stringify ARRAY `["sd-file-version:v1", assetId, contentSha256, completeness, sourceVersionLabel, sourceStageLabel, amendsVersionId, amendmentReason]`; object tags use exactly the property insertion order shown above. Store the complete tuple and versionKey. Duplicate versionKey compares every incoming immutable capture field INCLUDING bytecount/mediaType/source/scope/correction tuple; mismatch409 `DOCUMENT_VERSION_CONFLICT`. Server-generated versionId/storageKey/capturedAt/createdByUserId belong to the winning FIRST observation and are not compared to a freshly generated retry value or overwritten on retry. Current caller authorization is checked independently on each retry. Identical bytes with changed source stage/completeness/correction may be a new version; no dedupe by filename or hash alone.

Mutable operational version fields are separately named: validation `{state:"quarantined|validated|rejected",evidenceRef:null|string}`; publication `{state:"unreleased|released|legacy_access_unknown",evidenceRef:null|string}`; stateRevision integer>=0. They are not mutable immutable-capture fields. An append-only transition audit records each operational change; no caller can set them in upload bodies. A future legacy bridge alone may produce legacy_access_unknown using its frozen approved dataset; it cannot relabel new unverified uploads as legacy.

Create-only correctness indexes: FileAsset `{identityKey:1}` UNIQUE; FileAssetVersion `{assetId:1,versionKey:1}` UNIQUE; FileAssetVersion `{assetId:1,_id:-1}` for listing; FileDocumentAudit `{operationId:1,phase:1}` UNIQUE. Mongo _id uniqueness supplies version ID uniqueness. Before writes, verify exact key/options/index readiness through a read-only port; absent/mismatched503 `DOCUMENT_STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE`. Root F13/C2 controls actual index installation; no startup syncIndexes/autoIndex/deleting duplicates. An index declaration is not runtime evidence.

## First-increment commands and exact private DTOs

Routes added under the EXISTING authenticated `/api/v1/file` mount:

- `POST /assets/uploads` creates/reuses an unbound private_attachment. Query exactly `documentKey`; one multipart field `file`; no metadata/module/recordId/body owner fields.
- `POST /clinical/:resourceKind/:resourceId/uploads`, kind booking|external_booking, uses the owned scope resolver before parsing and otherwise the same upload protocol.
- `GET /assets/:assetId/versions`, query exactly optional `limit` canonical decimal1..50(default20) and `after` lowercase24hex; duplicates/arrays/unknown keys400.
- `GET /assets/:assetId/versions/:versionId/content`, no query parameters; authenticated same-owner/private or released-clinical bytes according to the table below.
- `POST /assets/:assetId/revoke`, JSON exactly `{expectedRevision:number,operationId:UUIDv4}`; unbound private_attachment owner only in this increment.

Ordered upload admission: authenticate; actor shape/kind; closed route/query and documentKey; current trusted owner scope; storage/index readiness; multipart parse/type/size; derive identity and read/create asset; immutable version capture. Upload request fields must be checked after formidable parsing as well as route validation. Exactly one file,10MiB actual streamed ceiling, at most4KiB parsed nonfile fields, max original filename128UTF8bytes,30s upload deadline; preserve no temporary file supplied by the client. Input invalid400 `DOCUMENT_INPUT_INVALID`, unsupported actual media415 `DOCUMENT_MEDIA_UNSUPPORTED`, size413 `DOCUMENT_TOO_LARGE`. Unknown/application-octet-stream or declaration/content mismatch is unsupported. Detect actual supported magic/header, not extension; do not claim a header check is malware validation. Temporary parser files stay in the owned bounded private staging subtree, cleaned by exact admission-owned identity only; no raw formidable default tmpdir.

Upload returns201 only after asset/version/audit metadata commit; exact duplicate observation returns200. Envelope `{success:true,data:VersionDTO}`. VersionDTO has EXACT fields `{assetId,versionId,resourceKind,resourceId,purpose,mediaType,byteLength,capturedAt,completeness,validationState,publicationState,isCurrentReadable,contentUrl}`. IDs lowercase; capturedAt canonical ISO UTC; contentUrl exact local authorized content route when readable for this actor, otherwise null. No hashes, disk paths, original/provider URLs, raw payloads, patient identifiers beyond the authorized resource, scan details or evidence secrets. JSON serialization is bounded64KiB; overflow503 `DOCUMENT_STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE` before response.

List returns200 `{success:true,data:{assetId,versions:VersionDTO[],nextCursor:string|null}}`; no total count. Query by exact assetId, `_id < after` when supplied, sort `_id:-1`, limit+1 under2000ms. Validate returned scalar identity/asset/resource/state and row budget before DTO projection; malformed data503 `DOCUMENT_STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE`, no partial page. Seek pagination does not promise a whole-history snapshot; concurrent new versions can appear on a fresh first page. All owned versions, including quarantined/rejected metadata, are visible to the owner; their unreadable contentUrl remains null. Historical released/eligible versions remain available when the current pointer changes, subject to current resource authority/revocation; isCurrentReadable is informative, never sole authority for all history. No arbitrary query/selection/sort/disk-key input.

Private errors and JSON/bytes use `Cache-Control: private, no-store`, `Pragma: no-cache`, `Vary: Authorization`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`. Missing/foreign/revoked assets or mismatched version IDs404 `DOCUMENT_NOT_FOUND`; invalid grammar400; stored scope drift503 `DOCUMENT_SCOPE_CHANGED`; validation/release unavailable503 `DOCUMENT_NOT_AVAILABLE`; policy adapter unavailable503 `DOCUMENT_POLICY_UNAVAILABLE`; persistence/audit failure503 `DOCUMENT_STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE`; expected revision/CAS/identity mismatch409 `DOCUMENT_VERSION_CONFLICT`. Return no filesystem exception details. HEAD uses the same authorization/state/audit/hash path but sends no body; Range requests416 with no partial bytes. No 304/public ETag/Last-Modified/private-object redirects.

## Frozen purpose/state/actor readability and eligibility ports

For every private command/read, resolve current asset scope and require exact signed user owner. This is an admission decision per request, not continuous cancellation of bytes already in flight. A role label, stored URL or unbound uploader ID never grants another resource's clinical authority.

| Purpose and association | Versions-list metadata | Actual content |
| --- | --- | --- |
| private_attachment + unbound_upload, same owner | All nonrevoked owned versions | validated AND unreleased is readable to its uploader; no clinical release asserted |
| clinical_document + owned booking/external_booking | All nonrevoked owned versions after current scope check | validated AND released; OR separately admitted legacy_access_unknown whose exact migration/access dataset currently permits that owner |
| either purpose, quarantined/rejected | Owner may see closed metadata |503 DOCUMENT_NOT_AVAILABLE, no descriptor opened |
| foreign/missing/revoked/mismatched association |404 |404, no descriptor opened |
| public_image or unsupported staff/caregiver/purpose | Excluded from first increment | No public/private bypass;403 actor denial or503 policy unavailable at internal service boundary |

Trusted internal `ValidationPort.evaluate` input is immutable `{assetId,versionId,contentSha256,actualSize,mediaType}` plus its owned read-only descriptor capability. Result is `{decision:"validated"|"rejected"|"unavailable",evidenceRef:null|boundedOpaqueId}` bound to those exact bytes. This port has no client-body equivalent; missing/unavailable adapter preserves quarantine, never defaults clean. Apply a successful result only with exact asset/version/hash, expected stateRevision and current asset revision/owner scope; persist evidence reference and transition audit atomically. Reject/explain stale results409 rather than reusing another version's scan. Sanitizing, scanning, supported files and real configured evidence remain activation facts; fixture outcomes prove only the fixture protocol.

Trusted internal `ReleaseEligibilityPort.evaluate` input is `{assetId,versionId,contentSha256,resourceKind,resourceId,ownerUserId,expectedAssetRevision,expectedStateRevision}`. Result is `{decision:"eligible"|"denied"|"unavailable",evidenceRef:null|boundedOpaqueId}`. Its actual future adapter MUST establish current qualified signatory/assignment/consent and the allowed preliminary/correction recipients. No adapter exists by implication here. Missing/unavailable returns503 DOCUMENT_POLICY_UNAVAILABLE and keeps clinical publication unreleased. An eligible result applies only if the same scope/hash/revisions and validated state still hold; metadata publication/readable pointer/audit commit together. Denied cannot promote. There is NO HTTP release/validate or arbitrary admin boolean in this increment. Reader verifies persisted bound validation/publication evidence exists rather than calling a network scanner or release provider synchronously.

Thus private uploader retrieval has real behavior independent of clinical signatory release once validation succeeds. New clinical ingestion is still an acquisition/quarantine prerequisite; it is NOT a completed clinical workflow while genuine scanner/eligibility adapters are missing. Full S1 requires actual eligible release/authorized readability and existing client behavior, rather than passing permanent503 as module completion.

## Transaction, pointer, audit and detach ownership

FileDocumentService owns its Mongo session using the same concrete model connection for asset, version and audit repositories. Do not accept req.session, caller raw filters, foreign client sessions or a fake default transaction. Expose no raw session parameter publicly. The repository's internal session capability is created per command and used for every related write; source/runtime evidence must prove one connection/session and transaction lifecycle. Session closes in finally. Driver errors propagate to the classified boundary; no catch-as-success or fallback writes. A duplicate-key race aborts that transaction; only after abort may a fresh bounded transaction read/reconcile the exact winning identity. Do not continue reads in an aborted session.

Allocate logical identity, operationId, candidate versionId/storageKey/capturedAt ONCE before withTransaction so callback retry does not create new identities/bytes. New asset revision0 is inserted with null pointers; capture transaction inserts/reuses version and sets currentCapturedVersionId using exact `_id,owner,identityKey,revision,revokedAt:null` predicate, incrementing revision once; create/retry compares the full tuple. Pointer updates return exact result and failure throws409 INSIDE the callback. CurrentReadableVersionId stays null for new quarantine. Validation of private_attachment can set it to that version in the same conditional transaction; clinical release can set it only after eligible validated publication. Old version bytes/capture fields never change. Duplicate successful upload reuses existing version/pointers and returns200 without incrementing or making an older retry the newest pointer. Operation replay does not duplicate transition audit. A rejected/unavailable scan creates no readable pointer.

Audit schema is closed `{operationId,phase,actorUserId,resourceKind,resourceId,assetId,versionId,outcome,createdAt,correlationId,byteCount}` (versionId is nullable; byteCount is null except a read_finished nonnegative safe integer bounded10MiB) with server-assigned bounded values; phase enum capture|validation|release|read_admitted|read_finished|revoke. Outcome enum captured|validated|rejected|released|admitted|completed|disconnected|failed|revoked; only the matching phase/outcome pairs are admitted. operationId collision/replay compares actor/resource/asset/version/phase and the original immutable result before reuse; a foreign operation ID409 never exposes another owner's receipt. No patient payload, hash, file URL, raw error or source credential. Mutating domain/audit records commit in the SAME Mongo transaction. Audit failure aborts the mutation; private orphan files may remain unreachable. Read admission rechecks current scope/state, records durable read_admitted BEFORE opening/releasing bytes, and fails503 if that write fails. read_finished records completed|disconnected|failed plus bounded server byte count after streaming; a post-byte failure cannot retract delivery, so read_admitted remains incomplete and failure is recorded as unresolved by the existing sanitized error boundary. Never report zero exposure when bytes already streamed. No long database transaction spans an HTTP stream, and no operational log can replace a required durable admission event.

Revoke is ONLY same-owner unbound private_attachment: expectedRevision exact nonnegative safe integer, operationId exactUUIDv4; close body shape/actor before lookup, then owned lookup. Within one same-session transaction set revokedAt once, null readable pointer, increment asset revision and write revoke audit with operation ID. Same operation replay returns200 `{success:true,data:{assetId,revoked:true,revision}}` from its immutable recorded result after identity comparison; stale new operation409. No file/version delete, owner reassignment or promotion. Clinical detach, clinical revoke/retention holds and public withdrawal are EXCLUDED until their real policy/actor bindings freeze; internal calls return503 DOCUMENT_POLICY_UNAVAILABLE. The full S1 later replaces physical BookingDocumentService deletion with authorized reference-detach/retention, without using this unbound-only command as clinical deletion authority.

## Implementable Node filesystem algorithm and explicit threat boundary

Use a single configured upload root (the existing CONFIG-resolved root) and reserved child `__private_assets_v1`, owned by the service OS uid, root/private-directory0700 and files0600. Root is provisioned/configured by the local/deployment operator, not supplied by the HTTP request. The threat boundary excludes a malicious same-uid process/administrator capable of replacing that root or mutating held inode contents: Node's path APIs do not provide a portable openat2 directory-descriptor containment primitive. Do NOT claim lstat+O_NOFOLLOW defeats an adversary replacing arbitrary ancestors concurrently. A deployable root requires restrictive parent permissions and exclusive application ownership; multi-host/shared-NFS writers are unsupported until separately reviewed. No mkdir/chmod/inventory runs in preparation.

New storage keys use only server-generated lowercase24hex asset/version IDs and32byte randomhex filename; reject any manifest key not matching the fixed grammar. Initialization/admission lstat and realpath the trusted root/reserved child; require actual directories, expected uid/mode, no symlink and record dev/ino. Existing hostile/foreign paths fail503; never adopt/chmod them to make admission pass. Revalidate those identities before each storage operation and after completion; drift fails closed. This detects drift but cannot make stronger guarantees against the excluded hostile same-uid ancestor race.

Creation uses safe generated child directories, mode0700; new files opened `O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW`, mode0600. fstat verifies regular/nlink1/uid/mode and holds that fd while streaming bounded input, hashing/counting actual bytes, fsyncing and closing. Reopen read-only/no-follow under the same root identity, verify full bytes/hash/size and file identity before metadata publication. Never write existing keys, follow client symlinks, reuse a parser path as a final key or adopt an existing file on EEXIST. Failed capture remains an unreachable owned orphan, never an attached available document.

For content read, after metadata/state/audit admission, open the fixed storage key read-only O_NOFOLLOW; fstat require regular/nlink1/owner/mode/size. FIRST pass over that HELD descriptor computes full SHA256 and bytecount using bounded64KiB reads, validating declared media type and immutable metadata; fstat before/after hashing must match dev/ino/size/mtime/ctime. No response body bytes before this check. SECOND pass streams the SAME descriptor from position0 using explicit positions/chunk bounds, max10MiB,30s deadline/disconnect cleanup; verify descriptor identity again at end. Root/manifest/file mismatch503 before first byte, or terminate connection and retain failed audit if discovered after transmission. Do not silently reopen by path after verification. Auth admission and inode checks cannot revoke already transmitted bytes or defeat the excluded hostile same-uid in-place write during the second pass; immutable permissions and sole-writer behavior are deployment assumptions, honestly measured in fixtures.

Minimal existing-path isolation is required before NEW private files can exist: FileController's common static/fetch/structured/info resolver rejects any canonical path within the reserved subtree BEFORE existence/stat/read, including alternate encodings and normalized aliases. Never rely on obscurity or extension. FileService generic upload accepts only a flat `[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}` module other than reserved subtree and an optional exact24hex recordId before filesystem work; any unsupported old caller is a visible compatibility failure, not path escape permission. deleteFile similarly admits only canonical contained legacy paths, forbids the reserved subtree and symlinks/outside-root resolutions, and cannot erase new private files. Existing public-image return fields/URL generation and ordinary allowed-module writes stay unchanged. The trusted-root boundary applies to these legacy isolation checks too; tests must verify no remote request can create/replace the reserved ancestors through old module/record inputs.

## Pending S1 phases, not first-increment implementation admission

1. **Full clinical/static compatibility:** migrate available legacy references/bytes using exact owned resource/provenance datasets; record versionHistory unknown, not invented recovered history. Canonical resource-scoped old URLs must not authorize a different booking when copied. Full static/fetch/info aliases dispatch through authoritative purpose/access metadata; no arbitrary filesystem fallback may remain. Old clinical public caches/downloads need separate exposure handling. First-increment new-private-subtree denial does NOT fix all old public reports.
2. **Explicit public-image writers and client adapters:** USER profile uses UserModel and existing self-edit boundary; PHARMACY profile uses PharmacyModel and actual operational-owner guard; shared medicine imagery uses MedicineModel and its actual admin/shared-master guard, not arbitrary imageUrl. These are candidate future mappings, UNFROZEN/EXCLUDED now: no new public upload endpoint, publication role, field writer or URL rewrite is admitted by this contract. Freeze exact current writer/model/guard/response adapters in that phase before source changes; merely naming the models is not approval. Legacy public image inventory must bind canonical path, hash/type/size, publication resource and reviewed provenance. A filename suffix, generic profile URL or role string never proves publication. Fresh explicit public-image publication may not promote/copy an existing private asset. Preserve genuine existing images/remote image URLs and supported app/web rendering; no generic file gateway remains open permanently as a compatibility excuse.
3. **Provider/booking immutable adapter bridge:** replace BOTH explicit diagnostics fetch and stable callback filenames; map stable local resource+integration+provider-account+source document identity BEFORE asset lookup; integrate current arrays via exact version handles without losing original versions. Unauthenticated callbacks cannot mark available/released. Freeze provider destination/DNS-to-connection/TLS/redirect contracts, streamed10MiB/20s bounds and no ambient proxy; unknown signed CDN hosts503, no invented allowlist from API base URL. New provider source identity labels, account scope, token/correction mappings and actual supplied metadata are explicit prerequisites and excluded from this first increment.
4. **Qualified clinical flow and retention:** actual scanner/eligibility adapters, trusted lab/staff/signatory/assignment/consent/preliminary/correction policy, clinical detach/revoke/retention, current-permitted legacy bridge and audit/client adoption. Actual authorized content success is required, not only quarantined upload503s. Root owns technical compatibility/activation choices; technical delegation cannot fabricate a qualified signatory, consent fact, provider host or legacy inventory.

## Focused acceptance and gates

Exact source reviews bind the first-increment file list and method changes plus required complete relevant imports. No current application/Node/compiler/DB/Docker/provider/model/Ruflo invocation follows from this draft. Actual checks need complete pre-import C3; F13 index/connection/storage readiness is separately admitted. Source checks, fake ports and real DB/filesystem outcomes retain their actual scope.

Required focused cases: stable same resource/documentKey→same asset; identical version replay→same version without pointer/revision/audit mutation; different owner/resource/document/integration remains separate; equal hash but changed source labels/correction preserves both. Exercise recorded versus unknown labels, identity/hash collision mismatch, immutable retry timestamp/actor preservation, unique-index race/transaction abort and same-session CAS rollback. Test quarantined metadata visibility versus denied bytes; validated unbound same-uploader content success; foreign/revoked404; bound clinical denied without actual release; a trusted admitted fixture release yields actual authorized exact-version bytes while stale/forged release proof fails. This fixture is not qualified-owner acceptance.

Verify exact DTO/limit+1 seek pagination/unknown-key/error/cache/HEAD/Range behavior, resource ownership refresh, historical reads and pointer semantics, read audit pre-byte failure and post-byte unresolved outcome. Revoke only unbound owner, CAS/replay results, no physical erase and no clinical-revoke route.   - **Where:** file/controller:93 calls `applyPrivateDocumentHeaders(res)` unconditionally at the top of `uploadFiles`.
  - **Effect:** every legacy POST /upload and /upload/:module response, successes included, now carries:
    - private Cache-Control, Pragma, `Vary: Authorization` and nosniff;
    - validator stripping and deletion of the request's conditional headers.
  - **Why it matters:**
    - The core contract says these adapters change only their path guards and remain byte-preserved.
    - The addendum and the remediation both say legacy image handling is unchanged.
    - Practical risk is small for a POST JSON response, but this is the legacy image header effect the packet excludes.
  - **Minimal fix:** drop :93 and apply the helper only when `legacyUploadScope` or `legacyPath` denies: catch the `DOCUMENT_*` AppError around `fileService.uploadFiles`, apply the headers, then rethrow.
  - **Check:** compare baseline and current headers for a successful legacy upload, and confirm that a reserved-subtree module denial still carries the private headers.
- **R11-F2-2 LOW: Formidable input errors are misclassified.**
  - **Where:** storage:151-153 (`cancel`) and :249-252 (the catch) turn every error that is neither an AppError nor httpCode 413 into a 503 DOCUMENT_STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE.
  - **Effect:**
    - Formidable 3.x tags a malformed multipart body, a missing boundary and an empty file with httpCode 400. Clients therefore get a retry-inviting 503 instead of 400 DOCUMENT_INPUT_INVALID.
    - maxFiles, maxFields and maxFieldsSize carry 413 and become DOCUMENT_TOO_LARGE, while the contract treats "exactly one file and no fields" as a 400 case.
  - **Minimal fix:**
    - map httpCode 400 to 400 DOCUMENT_INPUT_INVALID;
    - keep 413 only for the file-size codes;
    - map the count and field limits to 400;
    - leave unknown codes as 503.
  - **Checks:** a bad boundary, a truncated body, an empty file, two files, and one or two extra fields.
- **R11-F2-3 LOW: the clinical route accepts `unbound_upload`.**
  - **Where:** controller:67 forwards `req.params.resourceKind`, and documents.ts:40 admits all three kinds.
  - **Effect:** POST /clinical/unbound_upload/<anything>/uploads silently becomes an unbound private upload and never validates `:resourceId`.
    - There is no authority change: owner, purpose and identity are the same as /assets/uploads.
    - However, the contract fixes this route's resourceKind to booking or external_booking.
  - **Minimal fix:** `uploadClinicalAsset` rejects any other kind with 400 before calling `upload`.
  - **Check:** that URL returns 400 with zero storage or database effects.
- **R11-F2-4 LOW (conditional): reserved-subtree alias on case-folding filesystems.**
  - **Where:** storage:31 compares `part.toLowerCase()` with `__private_assets_v1`, and the lstat walk (:38-47) rejects only symlinks.
  - **Trigger:** a directory that applies Unicode case folding: ext4 or f2fs casefold, and possibly case-insensitive APFS. There, `__private_aſſets_v1` names the private root, because U+017F folds to `s` but `toLowerCase` leaves it unchanged.
  - **Effect:** that alias reaches the private root through /api/static, /fetch and deleteFile.
  - **Mitigations:** reading or deleting still needs the 256-bit random object filename, and default Linux ext4 is unaffected.
  - **Why it still matters:** the contract requires rejecting normalized aliases and not relying on obscurity.
  - **Minimal fix:** record the reserved directory's dev:ino, which `roots()` already derives, and reject in legacyPath any existing path component whose lstat dev:ino matches it. Alternatively, reject non-ASCII segments.
  - **Check:** a fixture directory with casefold enabled.

INFO:

- **Cleanup errors (storage:253-273).** An exception during cleanup (drift in `directory(lstat(staging))`, or a close or unlink failure) replaces the original error or a completed capture. This fails closed and keeps the orphan, but loses the original 400, 413 or 415 code.
- **Errors after bytes are sent.** `privateRequest` destroys the response, then errorHandler attempts to write JSON on it and Express falls back to finalhandler. Benign, but it logs a secondary error.
- **Audit schema (file/model:30-35)** has no enum or pairing for phase and outcome; only the typed call sites constrain them.
- **Audit attribution.** The internal `releaseVersion` and `validateVersion` record the asset owner as the audit actor. A future signatory or scanner adapter must supply its own accountable actor.
- **Legacy compatibility to inventory before activation:**
  - legacyPath (storage:27, :38-47) now refuses decoded names containing `% ? # ~` or control characters, and any symlinked path component, including a symlinked UPLOAD_DIR.
  - `roots()` needs a non-symlink, service-owned root with mode 0700, while FileService creates the root with the default mode. Private storage therefore fails closed until the root is provisioned.
- **Content-type test:** the upload content-type check is case-sensitive (documents.ts:50).
- **Outside the header contract, as stated:** parser errors raised before the mount, and `app.options('*', cors())` preflights.
- **Type-check focus (NOT_RUN):** the `as Response['end']` cast over the overloaded `end`, and the typing of the `res.req` header deletion.

Retained limits:

- Legacy public clinical static paths remain open.
- No scanner, qualified-release or readiness adapter exists yet.
- The filesystem threat boundary excludes a hostile same-uid process.
- A pending syscall or an admitted commit cannot be cancelled.
- Full S1, client and cutover gates remain.

## R11-3 Contact-index evaluator and native reader: APPROVE_SOURCE_ONLY
Verified:

- **Manifest:** recursively frozen, exact data.
- **Evaluator (contactIndexReadiness)** imports only util, buffer and the manifest.
  - It copies the manifest first and deep-compares it.
  - All copies go through own data descriptors. Proxies, accessors, symbols, cycles and foreign prototypes are rejected, within 8192 nodes, depth 16 and 262144 JSON bytes.
  - It checks the exact observation shape, budgets and binding.
  - A non-COMPLETE observation returns its declared failure code.
  - A COMPLETE observation must have:
    - 2 to 6 commands, confirmed cleanup, an ended session and exhausted cursors;
    - the exact listCollections row: options limited to collation, and info containing only readOnly:false and the bound UUID;
    - every index row exactly `{spec}`, where any build marker denies by its presence;
    - only ordinary numeric specs within the frozen option set, plus the exact retained `name_text`, which is the only string-key form;
    - an `_id_` that agrees with idIndex in v, options and collation, and the presence of `name_text`;
    - the exact named, unique, partial contact index with no sparse, hidden or TTL option;
    - an effective collation that is either explicitly simple, or absent with an observed simple default.
  - Only READY sets metadataReady.
- **Reader binding:**
  - Takes zero arguments and is pinned to mongoose 6.13.8.
  - Checks User model, Connection, native Db, MongoClient, wrapper and native collection identity through own data properties and prototype getters. It never reads the URL or credentials.
  - Requires the client profile: direct connection, retryReads false, pool size 1, every timeout ≤250 ms.
  - Owns one session with causalConsistency false, and re-checks identity before every command and before cleanup.
- **Reader commands:**
  - The only commands are:
    - a literal listCollections filtered to the exact name;
    - a UUID-targeted listIndexes with includeIndexBuildInfo;
    - at most four getMores using the held native Long;
    - one exact killCursors.
  - They run with read preference primary, promoteLongs and promoteBuffers false, and UTF-8 validation on.
  - Acquisition stops at 4 s, and no acquisition command starts with less than 1 s before that cutoff. Cleanup ends by 5 s, and no cleanup command starts with less than 500 ms left. There is no retry.
- **Reader BSON copy:**
  - Native Long, Timestamp and Binary values are admitted only at their declared transport paths.
  - The native UUID prototype is admitted only at `cursor/firstBatch/N/info/uuid`, and only with exactly four fields, `__id` undefined, subtype 4 and 16 bytes. It is rebuilt as a fresh Binary.
  - Logical size is accumulated per element and must equal `calculateObjectSize` of the owned copy.
- **Reader results:**
  - An unsupported row fails the whole observation (UNSUPPORTED) rather than being filtered out.
  - The listing is capped at 64 rows: a 65th row or a non-terminal empty batch fails, and no prefix is ever reported COMPLETE.
  - A returned cursor is captured before any copy-time failure, so it can still be killed.
  - Uncertain or unconfirmed cleanup is reported as FAILED/CLEANUP_UNCONFIRMED.
  - The result is frozen, and the module is not imported anywhere.

INFO and checks:

- **R11-F3-1 INFO (check).** header() requires `cursor.ns === <db>.users` (reader ~L198), and getMore and killCursors target `users` (~L257, ~L302).
  - Historically some servers reported listIndexes cursors as `<db>.$cmd.listIndexes.<coll>`.
  - If Mongo 8.0.x does that, every run fails closed with CURSOR_INCOMPLETE and never reaches READY.
  - Confirm the actual reply form in the admitted fixture, including a multi-batch case.
- **R11-F3-2 INFO.** After an uncertain command, CLEANUP_UNCONFIRMED overwrites the primary failure code. This matches the contract but loses the diagnostic.
- **R11-F3-3 INFO.** Wildcard keys such as `{"$**":1}` without wildcardProjection pass as ordinary unrelated rows. They can never satisfy the contact requirement.
- **Retained limits:**
  - metadataReady does not mean all-account, backfill or all-writer coverage, legacy ownership or activation.
  - There is no socket cancellation and no pre-decoder heap bound.
  - The User schema does not yet declare contactKeys or its index. Until the identity writer exists, new single-contact users fall outside the partial index.
